items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Jack Butler, Johnny (Bugs) Hamilton, Fats regular trumpet man and myself, were the brass section.

ctx.x: I had not been with Kirk's orchestra a very long time, but I did enjoy every moment of my stay. It was probably the kind of band that he'd had for years back. It had the real Kansas City feeling, which a lot of the bands in the East did not have. Benny Carter certainly did not have it, though possibly Teddy Hill came closer to it. It's difficult to define what the Kansas City "feeling" was. The only thing I can say is that their approach to jazz was centered on "swing", which was always the first consideration.…

I started getting some gigs and some of them were with the great Fats Waller who was doing theatre dates of from one to three days in small towns in the States of New York, Massachusetts, Connecticut and New Jersey. Dave McRae, an alto player, was the one who engaged some of the musicians for the big band that Fats was using: Jack Butler, Johnny (Bugs) Hamilton, Fats regular trumpet man and myself, were the brass section. Herb Fleming on trombone, Cordic Wallace, bass, Al Casey, guitar, Arthur Tappier, drums, Bob…

Fats was a natural hit everywhere we played. As "Bugs" Hamilton had been with Fats a long time, he was normally the leader of the trumpet section because he had parts that he played when Fats only used a small combo. He would give Jack and myself the solos that he didn't care about playing. Sometimes when his lips were not feeling too strong, Bugs would ask me or Jack to take a solo in numbers that he enjoyed playing.
